guide: Use Claude Code in a terminal to sort the files on an old laptop and a Google Drive, while keeping a folder of files you review and delete yourself. You need Claude Code installed, a laptop with files to sort, and Google Drive for desktop so your Drive appears as a normal folder.
1. Install Claude Code from Anthropic and open a terminal in the folder you want tidied, such as Documents or Downloads.
1. Install Google Drive for desktop so your Drive shows up as a folder on the laptop that Claude Code can read.
1. Ask Claude Code to list what is there first: file types, sizes, duplicates and anything it cannot identify, without moving anything yet.
1. Create a folder called "To Be Deleted" and tell Claude Code to move files it thinks are junk or duplicates into it rather than deleting them.
1. Ask Claude Code to sort the remaining files into clear folders by type or project, and to explain each rule before it applies it.
1. Repeat the same process on your external hard drives, one at a time, with each drive plugged in.
1. Open "To Be Deleted" yourself, look through it, and delete what you are sure about.
Watch out: never give Claude Code permission to delete files, because the "To Be Deleted" folder is what keeps every final decision with you.
